audit.why: Levels 1-5 belong to Ahri: Orb of Deception (970 range, 7s) outranges Breath of Light (750) and Charm (975, 12s) cancels the channel. Aurelion Sol only stabilises once Rod of Ages/Seraph's lands and the stardust curve bends. Packet chart (Ahri x5, Aurelion Sol x2) agrees with win[]/phases[].side, so no chart flip proposed.
audit.corrected: Chart left as-is; difficulty 7/10 retained against a 46.37% win rate over 1393 games.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] named 'Shadowflame or Liandry's' as the first item, contradicting the full layer's Rod of Ages/Seraph's line, and credited 'W stun' — Astral Flight (W) is a flight over terrain, the stun is Falling Star (R). spikes[3] invented a 'global Comet threat' and a '5-star ult'.
audit.why: Aurelion Sol's only stun is R (120/110/100s). W has no CC. Comet is a rune, not a global threat.
audit.corrected: First-item spike keyed to RoA/Seraph's plus stacked Breath of Light; late spike keyed to The Skies Descend.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere stated the decisive interaction: Breath of Light (Q) and Astral Flight (W) are both interruptible channels and Charm (E) cancels either one.
audit.why: brief.missingInteractions rule 'your-channel-punished'; ownerKit flags channel: 'interruptible — any CC cancels it' on both Q and W; Ahri E flag hardCC.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now states Charm is 12s flat and cancels the beam, so you channel only after it is spent. Orb of Deception's return leg dealing true damage (resistances do not help) added to the early text.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns carried no real numbers and a templated 'fifth summoner spell' line.
audit.why: Charm 12s, Astral Flight 22s at rank 1, R 120s at rank 1 make the advice concrete.

audit.whatIsWrong: early/mid/late referenced a shield Aurelion Sol does not have and a 'W stun'.
audit.why: ownerKit has no shield flag on any slot; W is terrain-flight.
audit.corrected: Replaced with Falling Star and Astral Flight spacing.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d were pasted trade-template text that did not match their own titles.
audit.why: Template detection per the sweep: both sentences would fit any enemy with the name swapped.
audit.corrected: Grounded in Spirit Rush charges and Orb of Deception's true-damage return.

edits.before: Ahri wins by landing Charm, denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Ahri wins by landing Charm the moment you start a beam, then Spirit Rushing on top of the cancel for the burst.

edits.before: - Ahri Charm: matchup-defining — The charm starts every kill pattern — stay behind minions while it is up. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your W Astral Flight like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Ahri Charm: 12s flat — it starts every kill pattern and it cancels your Breath of Light channel, so beam only once it is spent. - Astral Flight is 22s at rank 1: it is your escape, never your poke. - Falling Star: 120s, kill windows only.

edits.before: Carry by scaling honestly — every stardust stack is permanent, and the 30-minute version of you wins fights your laning self cannot imagine.
edits.after: Carry by outliving Charm: it is her only lockdown and it is 12s, so survive one per rotation and the permanent stardust curve does the rest.

edits.before: W-flyby: fly a lateral arc, drag Q across Ahri for two seconds of burn + stacks, and land outside his answer range — repeat forever from one item.
edits.after: Falling Star stuns her out of Spirit Rush mid-dash, so hold it for the moment she spends all three charges on you, not for chip on a poking Ahri.

edits.before: Channelling Q face-to-face inside his engage range with W down — every champion that touches you wins that exchange pre-items.
edits.after: Charm plus Orb of Deception's true-damage return kills from further than you think — below half, stacks are not worth a 12s coin flip.

edits.before: Spirit Rush gives Ahri a three-dash burst combo you cannot out-position or shield through
edits.after: Spirit Rush gives Ahri three dashes to Charm, burst and reset before Falling Star lands

edits.before: Your first completed core item (usually Shadowflame or Liandry's) lets your Q poke and W stun start out-trading her sustained Orb of Deception harass.
edits.after: Your first core item (Rod of Ages or Seraph's) lets Breath of Light's stacked ticks out-trade her Orb of Deception, and Falling Star answers her all-in.

edits.before: Your global Comet threat and 5-star ult wipe teamfights and side lanes at once, something Ahri's single-target Charm chain can't answer.
edits.after: The Skies Descend drags a whole group in while your stacked Breath of Light melts them — Ahri's single-target Charm chain can't answer that.

edits.before: Ahri's Orb of Deception harasses you from a range your early Q arc can't answer, and she can walk it back through minions for a second tick while you're still building star count. Charm is the real threat: if she lands it near a minion wave you're dead to the Fox-Fire follow-up before your shield or W stun ever comes online. Play passive, hold your stacked star count for zoning rather than farming aggression, and never let your HP dip low enough that a landed Charm is lethal.
edits.after: Ahri's Orb of Deception harasses you from a range your early Q arc can't answer, and she pulls it back through minions for a true-damage second tick while you're still building star count. Charm is the real threat: if she lands it near a minion wave you're dead to the Fox-Fire follow-up long before Falling Star is unlocked. Play passive, hold your stacked star count for zoning rather than farming aggression, and never let your HP dip low enough that a landed Charm is lethal.

edits.before: Spirit Rush at 6 turns her from a poke champion into a three-dash execute threat — she can Charm you off a wall angle, dash in twice for Fox-Fire stacks, and reset out before your W stun ever lands. You're still surviving on Comet zoning and W peel rather than winning trades outright here. The moment either Charm or Spirit Rush is on cooldown is your only real all-in window; otherwise keep priority soft and deny roams with vision instead of forcing fights.
edits.after: Spirit Rush at 6 turns her from a poke champion into a three-dash execute threat — she can Charm you off a wall angle, dash in twice for Fox-Fire stacks, and reset out before your Falling Star ever lands. You're still surviving on Astral Flight spacing rather than winning trades outright here. The moment Charm (12s flat) or Spirit Rush is on cooldown is your only real all-in window; otherwise keep priority soft and deny roams with vision instead of forcing fights.

edits.before: Once you finish your core burst item your Q-into-W combo starts outpacing her charm-poke pattern, and by two items your global ultimate threatens both side lanes and teamfights in a way her Spirit Rush kit can't match. Play the objective map: use Comet to threaten drakes/Herald from lane, force her to either walk into your zone control or give up map presence. In teamfights, land Q on her first — Ahri without Charm available folds instantly to your ultimate.
edits.after: Once your first item lands, a held Breath of Light outpaces her charm-poke pattern, and by two items The Skies Descend swings objective fights in a way her Spirit Rush kit can't match. Play the objective map: park the black hole's execute on the approach to drakes, forcing her to walk into it or give up map presence. In teamfights, hold the beam on her first — Ahri without Charm available folds to a Falling Star stun.

notes: Aurelion Sol has no shield and no global ability; the content layer repeatedly attributed both to him ('shield or W stun', 'global Comet threat', 'use Comet to threaten drakes/Herald'), and treated the Arcane Comet rune as an ability. Fixed where the length band allowed. Ahri's Essence Theft (P) sustain means Grievous Wounds timing matters in extended trades, but no writable field had room to add it without displacing a grounded fact — left for a future pass. Level chart untouched: packet, phases[].side and win[] all agree.
